sources.exact_hypotheses_or_scope: Defines an algebraic torus over k as a group becoming a product of multiplicative groups G_m over an extension; split means already isomorphic to a product of G_m over k.
sources.exact_conclusion_or_content: Places split multiplicative-group geometry in the standard algebraic-torus framework; it does not state the project's tangent-concurrency quotient or off-diagonal restriction.

sources.citation: Columbia University GU4041 notes, The Cauchy-Frobenius Lemma.
sources.exact_hypotheses_or_scope: Finite group G acting on a finite set X.
sources.exact_conclusion_or_content: Orbit count is the average of fixed-point counts, |G\X|=(1/|G|) sum_g |X^g|; no project-specific eta(BC), eta(-BC) specialization is stated.

sources.citation: W. S. Chou, J. Gomez-Calderon, G. L. Mullen, Value sets of Dickson polynomials over finite fields, Journal of Number Theory 30(3) (1988), 334-344, DOI 10.1016/0022-314X(88)90006-6.
sources.exact_hypotheses_or_scope: Finite field F_q, Dickson polynomial g_d(x,a), arbitrary prime-power q as described in the article abstract.
sources.exact_conclusion_or_content: Determines the cardinality of the Dickson-polynomial value set over F_q; this is direct prior art for finite-field Dickson/Joukowski-type image counting, but the audited source text does not state the project's normalized lambda_s formula or s=3 extremal arithmetic closure.

sources.exact_hypotheses_or_scope: Dickson polynomial D_n(x,a) and any representation x=u+a/u where defined.
sources.exact_conclusion_or_content: States the classical functional identity D_n(u+a/u,a)=u^n+a^n/u^n and the Chebyshev relation; this directly exposes the involutive Joukowski/Dickson parameterization u<->a/u.

sources.citation: T. Brazelton, J. Harrington, M. Litman, T. W. H. Wong, Residue sums of Dickson polynomials over finite fields, Journal of Number Theory 264 (2024), DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2024.04.016.
sources.exact_hypotheses_or_scope: Dickson polynomials over finite fields of odd characteristic; article gives a complete characterization of value-set size and separates hyperbolic, elliptic, and parabolic regimes.
sources.exact_conclusion_or_content: Confirms the established literature has detailed hyperbolic/elliptic Dickson value-set analysis; it does not present the audited H1-H2-J1-J2-C1-C2 chain or the terminal 105/53 arithmetic closure.

sources.citation: O. Kucuksakalli, Value sets of Lattes maps over finite fields, Journal of Number Theory (2014), DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2014.04.014.
sources.exact_hypotheses_or_scope: Finite-field value sets; gives an alternative computation of Dickson-polynomial value sets using a singular cubic curve and generalizes to Lattes maps.
sources.exact_conclusion_or_content: Provides a geometric route to Dickson value sets, relevant as adjacent method rather than an exact duplicate of the project's split-hyperbola tangent-concurrency construction.
